procedure.step: The Ministry of Economy and Tourism registers the factory (outside a free zone) before applying for a certificate; registration takes about 3 working days.
procedure.authority: the Ministry of Economy and Tourism

procedure.step: The issuing authority may require detailed cost sheets and a factory visit; each item on the certificate must qualify separately.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade issues the certificate through the 'Certificate of Origin for India' e-service; processing takes about one working day.
The Ministry of Foreign Trade charges a certificate fee of AED 10 to AED 200 depending on the invoice value.
The competent authority issues the certificate before, at, or within 5 working days of export; it is valid for 12 months and covers one import.
The exporter ships the goods directly from the UAE to India; third-party invoicing is allowed if the exporter indicates it.
The Indian importer claims the CEPA rate when filing the bill of entry and keeps supporting documents for at least 5 years.
The exporter keeps origin records, including the cost breakdown, for at least 5 years from the end of the calendar year of issue.

caveats.note: No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty only; IGST, GST compensation cess, Social Welfare Surcharge and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
'+' in the rule is read as 'and' (both tests must pass); the agreement does not define '+', so this is Mansha's interpretation.
A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, which is required before applying for the certificate.
'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement.
Operations listed in the agreement as minimal (simple packaging, labelling, simple assembly, simple testing, etc.), alone or combined, never confer origin regardless of the product-specific rule.
